text:
Nic Dowd made his name as Washington's shutdown center, and Vegas brought him in to do the same job. At 36 he's still finishing checks (67 hits in 25 games), but his minutes have slipped to about 10 a night and the five-on-five results are hard to defend. He has three assists, no goals and eight shots on goal.

With Dowd on the ice, Vegas has had 37% of the expected goals (the quality of chances); without him, the Golden Knights are 20 points better. Bad luck is part of it: the team has scored 6.1 fewer goals than its chances deserved during his shifts, and that usually swings back. But the chances themselves are the problem, and that matches last season, when Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level (-1.1 wins) with his team creating little while he was out there (bottom 8% of forwards).

KTNV's morning segment had him sharing "words of wisdom" last week, and a veteran's voice counts for something in a young room. On the ice, watch the deployment. A center whose minutes keep shrinking and whose shifts tilt the wrong way is in a role that gets reviewed.
